items.description: A group kind — a policy bundle, never a size label. Every field here must be behavior-bearing: a kind that differs from another only in Capacity is a capacity value, not a kind, and WorldDefinitionValidator refuses that pair by name.

name.description: The kind's stable name, unique within Kinds — the vocabulary a KindName reference is validated against (unknown-by-name, the same shape as the state-row cell-existence refusal).

roles.description: The role→capability map (see WorldGroupRole). May be empty — a kind with no roles reaches no capability at all through its group principal, so any grant naming it is refused as unreachable.

items.description: One named role a WorldGroupKind declares — the role→capability half of the kind's policy bundle. A role names nothing about membership (this head keeps a membership row role-less; see Members); it exists so world.grant can refuse, at the door, a hold over a group principal that no role of its kind could ever exercise (the addon-reachability-honesty analog: an admitted-but- unreachable grant is a grant that lies).

name.description: The role's stable name, unique within its kind.

capabilities.description: The capabilities a member acting under this role may be granted through the group principal. Never empty — a role reaching nothing is a role that could not exist without lying about what it is for.

items.description: The coarse capability verbs a WorldGrant confers — the closed set the server checks a submission's WorldPrincipal against at each write boundary. A genre world arrives as different data (new subjects, new sections), never a new capability.

lifetime.description: The lifetime/persistence policy (see WorldGroupLifetime) — runtime groups only.

evictionPolicy.description: What a kick does to the kicked member's row — and, under Disband, to the whole group (see WorldGroupEvictionPolicy).

capacity.description: The maximum concurrent members a group of this kind admits — one minor authored field within MaxMembersPerGroup, the population ceiling this substrate is bounded against.

sharedStateScope.description: The name of a declared state row this kind's groups share, or null for none. Validated to reference an existing row (refused by name otherwise, the same cell-existence discipline the world-rules operand walk enforces) — the deeper "every member reads/writes this row together" semantic belongs to a later lane; this head only pins the reference honest.

groups.description: The group roster — authored and runtime rows in one list (see WorldGroup).

items.description: One group row — a roster of principals under a kind. One shape whether the row was boot-authored (present in the server's own base document — re-seeded on every world.reset/.load/.reload) or formed live by WorldMutation.FormGroup (never written back to the base, so a whole-document rebuild simply does not carry it forward — the party-vs-roster split falls out of the ordinary document-swap machinery, not a bespoke flag on this type).

id.description: The group's stable id, unique within Groups — the token Group carries as a grant principal. WorldSafeName-typed (the For precedent: a scoped session's process-local instance name is composed from this id, literal separators and all, in WorldSessionResolver.MintInstanceName — typing it here is what makes that composition injective by construction rather than by an escaping step downstream that could collapse two distinct ids onto one name).

kindName.description: The owning kind's name — validated to reference a declared WorldGroupKind (unknown-by-name).

members.description: The current membership — flat only: every entry is a principal, never a group (a Group entry is refused by name — a member holding another group's memberships by proxy is exactly what flat membership forbids), and never World/ Document (neither is a real actor a hold could ever reach). Bounded by the kind's own Capacity.

tags.description: The row's own tags — what a Tagged destination selector matches against: a traveler resolving a tagged destination is expected to hold exactly one membership among rows carrying the selector's tag, never zero or several. Validated non-empty and distinct when present; null/absent means this row carries none, which is not the same as an authored empty list (refused — omit the member instead).

ownership.description: The ownership bindings (see WorldOwnership). May be empty.

items.description: One ownership binding — subject → principal-or-group-or-escrow, the second kind of the group+binding substrate. A row is document-authored (boot/reset/load-seeded, like every other row in this section), but its Owner moves live through WorldMutation.OfferOwnership (owner -> escrow) and WorldMutation.SettleOwnership (escrow -> recipient, or escrow -> offerer on timeout) — the escrow/transfer lane, riding this exact row shape. There is still no mutation kind that creates a row from nothing (only a document may declare a subject's first owner) or that widens Kind past Group — a later lane adding item/instance subjects is expected to add whatever mints their first row, riding this same shape.

id.description: The subject's stable id — a group id for Group.

kind.description: Whether the owner is a bare principal, a group, or an escrow row.

principal.description: The owning principal for Principal; null otherwise. Never Group — a group owner is spelled through GroupId, not this field, so the two branches never overlap.

groupId.description: The owning group's id for Group; null otherwise.

escrow.description: The escrow payload for Escrow; null otherwise.

offerer.description: The principal that placed the subject into escrow — the sole reclaim beneficiary.

recipient.description: The principal named to accept the subject — the sole accept beneficiary. Never equal to Offerer (refused by name — an offer to oneself is not a trade).

deadlineTick.description: The server tick at or after which WorldMutation.SettleOwnership's reclaim admits — the same tick unit EpochTick already rides. Before this tick, only an accept by Recipient can resolve the escrow.
